books.section: Topic 4.13 The Society of the South in the Early Republic, C. Westward Expansion and the Politics of Slavery

primary_sources: Theodore Gentilz, Fall of the Alamo, 1844

stimulus.text: Theodore Gentilz painted this scene of the fall of the Alamo in 1844, eight years after the battle. The Alamo mission compound stands behind a wide open plain, and rows of soldiers stand in formation in the foreground.
stimulus.source_note: Painting viewed before writing: Theodore Gentilz, Fall of the Alamo, 1844, shared pool file u4/5s24-ch03-mcq-39.jpg, public domain. Gentilz painted the 1836 battle eight years after it happened; he was not an eyewitness.

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Theodore Gentilz, Fall of the Alamo, 1844, public domain
stem: Why had American settlers come to Texas in the 1820s and 1830s?

options.text: To farm cheap land for cotton, bringing enslaved people with them
To work in the factories Mexico built along the Rio Grande
options.misconception: Mexico built no factories for American settlers; the settlers came to farm.

options.text: To escape the cotton economy of the American South
options.misconception: The settlers came to extend the cotton economy, not to escape it.

options.text: To join the Mexican army and defend the Alamo
options.misconception: The settlers fought against the Mexican army at the Alamo, they did not join it.

rationales.A: Mexico offered abundant cheap land suited to cotton, and Southern settlers brought the plantation model and enslaved labor with them.
rationales.B: Mexico built no factories for American settlers. The settlers came to farm.
rationales.C: The settlers came to extend the cotton economy, not to escape it.
rationales.D: The settlers fought against the Mexican army at the Alamo, they did not join it.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what Texas offered. Mexico offered abundant cheap land that could grow cotton.
2. Ask who came. The settlers were mostly Southern whites who hoped to repeat the plantation model of the Old South.
3. Ask what they brought. They practiced slavery, even though Mexico had banned it.
Background: Mexico first welcomed the settlers as a buffer against Native raids, then tried to enforce its laws.
Remember: settlers carry their economy with them when they move.
